fields.features_heading: The Repeat Work Inside Every CRM
fields.features_subheading: CRM automation hands the clerical steps of a CRM to software, and reps keep the conversations that need a person.
fields.feature_1:
Assignment rules written as sentences

Your demo form asks for a state and a company size, and the rules you write turn those answers into an owner. Change a territory by describing the new split in a prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Two-way sync with the CRM you run

The app reads and writes contacts, deals, and tasks in HubSpot or any other CRM with an API. Reps keep working in the CRM they know, with no second system to keep current.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders that reach one named owner

Each reminder goes to the person who owns the record, in Slack, by email, or in the app. If the task is still open the next morning, the reminder escalates to their manager.
fields.feature_4:
A pipeline view that stays current

Open deals, stalled deals, and overdue tasks update on one dashboard while reps work. Every record and every change the automation makes is stored in a database you own.
fields.feature_5:
No task cap when a campaign lands

A trade show or a webinar can bring in a week's worth of leads in one afternoon. Each new lead is assigned and logged, and the automation keeps running with no task cap.
fields.feature_6:
The code behind your rules, yours to keep

Emergent exports the full code of the app, assignment rules included, to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Engineers can review each rule and change it in their own editor.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Automations Built Around One CRM
fields.tab_content_1:
Ohio demo requests land with the Midwest rep

Marisol Achterberg fills in the demo form for Kestrel Ridge Foods and picks Ohio as her state. The app creates her contact in HubSpot and assigns it to Desmond Okafor, because Ohio sits in his Midwest territory. Desmond gets a direct message in Slack with her name and the note she left on the form.
fields.tab_content_2:
Seven quiet days hand the owner a follow-up task

The $18,400 Brightwater Clinics deal has sat in Proposal for 7 days with no call, email, or meeting logged. The app adds a follow-up task due today for Anneliese Varga, who owns the deal, and emails her a link to it with the last note attached. The deal stays on the stalled list until she logs the next activity.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every Closed Won deal starts its onboarding

Teodor Haas marks the $32,000 Larchmont Freight deal Closed Won in HubSpot. An onboarding record opens with the deal value and goes to the account manager, Ruth Castellanos. Wendell Osei gets a kickoff form by email asking for his team's contacts and a start date. Nobody retypes the deal.
fields.tab_content_4:
Two records with one email wait for a merge

Renata Santos signs up for a webinar with an email already on her Vellum Print contact record. Instead of creating a second contact, the app holds the sign-up as a possible duplicate and sends both records to Hollis Brandvold in sales ops. He merges them in the app, and the sign-up lands on the original record.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan CRM automation around the work your reps repeat, then build it with Emergent and switch it on.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what reps do by hand
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Fix the fields the rules will read
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every task a rep does by hand in a week: copying form leads into the CRM, logging calls, chasing deals that went quiet. Count how often each one happens, and start with the task that repeats most and needs the least judgment.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Export your contacts and deals and check the fields each rule depends on, such as state and deal owner. A rule that reads an empty state field assigns nobody. Fill those gaps before you build anything.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe each rule the way you would brief a new rep. Leads from companies with over 500 employees go to the enterprise team; a deal moved to Negotiation alerts the sales manager. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the CRM and Slack through their APIs. Decide which system owns each fact: the CRM owns the deal stage and the owner, the form owns what the lead typed, and the app reads both.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Mark the changes a person approves
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the changes that should wait for a named person. Merging two contacts, moving a lead between reps, and editing a deal's value are good candidates, with both records shown beside the approve button.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Replay last month before going live
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's leads and deals through the automation before it writes to a live record. Check that each lead reached the right rep and that no deal got two tasks for one quiet stretch. Change a rule with a new prompt and replay the month.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Switch on one rule at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with lead assignment, since it writes only to new records. Track the hours from form fill to first call for 14 days and compare them with the 14 days before. Then add the next rule.

faq_plan.a: CRM automation is the use of technology and automation tools to handle repetitive tasks inside a customer relationship management system. The CRM holds the record of every current and prospective customer. The automation acts on those records: it assigns a new lead and creates the next task without a rep clicking through each step.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up CRM automation?
faq_plan.a: Describe the rules you want in Emergent's AI automation builder, one per sentence. Say which rep gets which leads, when a quiet deal earns a follow-up task, and what happens once a deal closes. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard and connects it to your CRM through its API. It is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What does an automated CRM do that a plain CRM does not?
faq_plan.a: An automated CRM acts when a record changes, without waiting for a rep to click. A plain CRM stores the lead and its history. The automated version also routes each prospect to a salesperson by criteria such as industry, company size, or location. It then creates the task or sends the alert that the change calls for.

faq_plan.q: What kinds of CRM automation tools are there?
faq_plan.a: CRM automation tools either run inside the CRM as its own workflow rules or sit outside it as a separate app connected through the CRM's API. Native rules handle steps inside one system. A separate app suits work that also touches a form or Slack. Nurture emails belong to a marketing automation workflow, which hands qualified contacts back to the CRM.

faq_plan.q: How does CRM workflow automation work?
faq_plan.a: CRM workflow automation runs on triggers and actions: a record changes, a rule checks it, and the app acts. A deal moving to Negotiation can trigger a message to the sales manager when its value is over $10,000. Chain several of those rules, and a workflow automation CRM setup can carry a deal from first form fill to the onboarding record with no copy and paste.

faq_plan.q: Can a sales automation CRM replace a sales rep?
faq_plan.a: No. CRM sales automation takes the clerical steps off a rep's day, such as data entry and reminders, while the calls and the negotiation stay with the rep. In an app built with Emergent, each automated step is recorded in a database you own, and a manager can see which steps the app took and which the rep took.

faq_plan.q: What can AI automation add to a CRM?
faq_plan.a: AI automation adds steps that work on free text, where a plain rule can only compare field values. It can summarize a long email thread onto the contact or draft a follow-up from the last call note. Rules still decide who owns a lead and which stage of your sales workflow a deal moves to next.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in CRM workflow automation software?
faq_plan.a: Look for software that reads and writes your CRM both ways, names an owner for every alert, and logs each action it takes. A CRM with workflow automation native to it covers steps inside the CRM, while outside software can also reach your inbox and forms. If it bills per task, a busy month costs more than a quiet one. Emergent builds the workflow as an app with no task cap.

faq_plan.q: Which part of a slow sales process should CRM automation fix first?
faq_plan.a: Find the stage where deals wait longest, and automate the work that keeps them waiting. Pull the average days each deal spends in each stage of your pipeline. If new leads wait hours for an owner, automate assignment. If proposals sit with no reply, add a follow-up task after a set number of quiet days, and give the rep the last note with it.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep two CRM automation rules from conflicting?
faq_plan.a: Give every field one rule that writes to it. If two rules both set the deal owner, the record ends up with whichever ran last. Keep a list of which rule writes which field, and merge two rules that need the same field into one rule with both conditions. Outreach steps such as email sequences belong in their own set of sales automation rules, apart from assignment.

plan.angle: The top 10 are CRM vendors and explainers that define the term and list generic automations inside their own product. findings.quote: Each new lead is assigned and logged, with no task cap and no overage line on the bill.
findings.issue: 'no overage line on the bill' is a pricing and billing guarantee about Emergent that is not in rules/capabilities.json (no-caps approves 'No task cap' only). Emergent bills in credits and the page's own table says AI steps 'share the same credit pool', so a busy campaign can cost more; the claim is unapproved and may be false. findings.fix: End at the approved claim, e.g. 'Each new lead is assigned and logged, and the app keeps running with no task cap.' (keep 165-182 chars), and do not add any billing or overage promise elsewhere.
